passages.note: Bill details page naming Mishler as the Senate sponsor of the enrolled act; it prints the digest, not the operative text.

passages.provision_quote: (4) For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022, and before January 1, 2025, three and fifteen hundredths percent (3.15%).
passages.note: Enrolled text of the bill he sponsored: it cuts the individual adjusted gross income rate for every taxpayer and repeals the utility receipts tax outright.
His Yea on the conference committee report, but the tally is 50-0, so under the near-unanimous rule this vote cannot carry the chair on its own.

rows.reasoning: Mishler was the Senate sponsor of HB 1002 (2022), whose enrolled text lowers the rate every individual taxpayer pays, to "three and fifteen hundredths percent (3.15%)" after 2022 with a further conditional phase-down, and repeals an entire tax ("SECTION 3. IC 6-2.3 IS REPEALED [EFFECTIVE JULY 1, 2022]. (Utility Receipts Tax)."). That is more than "targeted adjustments — closing loopholes or granting narrow relief" and it matches "Cut taxes broadly, including the main rates most people pay"; the rung above it is excluded because the act shrinks no government function and conditions the later cuts on revenue growth and pension funding. The chair rests on the sponsorship and the enrolled text, not on the 50-0 conference-report vote, which is near-unanimous.
